as_told.title: Doc Brown modeled on Townsend Brown, per his daughter

plain: The idea is that Doc Brown, the inventor in the film Back to the Future, is a quiet tribute to a real scientist named Thomas Townsend Brown, who did experiments with capacitors, devices that store electric charge, and whom people reportedly called "Doc Brown". Michels makes this case himself across several episodes: the film is set in 1985, which he says is the year Townsend Brown died, the character's full name is given as "E.M.T. Brown", and the film's "flux capacitor" echoes Brown's capacitor experiments. He credits the director Steven Spielberg with the nod, and in a 2026 episode he adds that he spoke to Brown's daughter directly, "who is sure that the character is based on him." If true, it would mean Hollywood was winking at a man Michels sees as a hidden pioneer of flying-craft research.
